chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from Ibn Fuddal, from Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from Hamzah ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, will hold evidence against the people with what He gave them and made them to recognize.
ai.seo_question: What is the basis of God's argument against humanity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq places this narration within the chapter on 'Recognition and Evidence' to establish that divine accountability is rooted in the internal faculties God endowed humans with, such as intellect and innate knowledge. This highlights the Shia concept of 'hujjah batinah' (inner evidence), where God's argument against humanity is not merely external revelation but also the cognitive and spiritual capacities granted to them. Consequently, human responsibility is derived from their ability to recognize and utilize these divine gifts.
